_about: The 12 English sample lines for the research-pipeline translation trial, copied verbatim from origin/main 1cf8d73. Each line carries the per-line context a translator gets (who speaks, where, what the player sees), its placeholders and the surface it renders on. Every trial tool reads this one file; nothing else lists the lines.

lines.context: Button on the END OF SLICE card. Starts a fresh run. All caps in English by design.

lines.text: No checkpoint yet. Saving starts at the first SAFE POINT.
lines.context: Title-screen note when Continue has nothing to load. SAFE POINT is the in-world name of the save station (glossary term).

lines.text: HOLD E: crank on, %d of %d, or let WOLF take the relay.
lines.context: Context hint above the dialogue bar while the engineer cranks the manual bypass. 'E' is the bound key (rebindable; the key name is swapped in by code later). The two %d are turns done and turns needed, in that order.

lines.text:
The sentry saw %s out in the open.
Stay close to the TANK RELEASE.
lines.context: Fail card after the sentry runs the engineer down. %s is the engineer's first name (Rowan, Alex or Morgan; any gender). TANK RELEASE is the station label the player can see (glossary term, must match L10). The line break is authored.

lines.text: The bypass handle is stiff. Coolant hisses from the relay housing and an alarm starts to wail.
lines.context: Narration box when the engineer first pulls the manual bypass handle. Present tense, terse, physical.

lines.text:
Nobody gives an activation command.
WOLF wakes himself.
lines.context: Opening cinematic caption. WOLF (a robotic wolf, he/him) wakes up on his own, without an order. The line break is authored.

lines.text: WOLF: That purge takes the original program logs. Once they're gone, his word is the only record.
lines.context: WOLF speaks to the engineer at the breaker. 'his' is the Director. 'WOLF: ' is the speaker tag the dialogue splitter reads; it is not translated.
lines.speaker: WOLF

lines.text: WOLF: At the relay you'd have sent me in blind. I won't walk into its sights. Time the drop from the release; it crosses the mark on every pass.
lines.context: WOLF refuses to lure the sentry because the engineer rushed him earlier at the relay. Calm, direct, not sulking. 'it' is the sentry; 'the release' is the TANK RELEASE station; 'the mark' is the floor spot under the tank.
lines.speaker: WOLF

lines.text: SENTRY  WOLF wouldn't draw it, so {name} timed the drop alone.
lines.context: End-card recap row. 'SENTRY' is the row's topic label, two spaces, then the summary. {name} is the engineer's first name (any gender; they/them in English). 'alone' must not reveal a gender.
Station plate over the lever that drops a coolant tank. 12 px caps on a small plate; must match the term used in L04.

lines.text: The relay may vent coolant. Your call.
lines.context: Answer button: the ENGINEER says this to WOLF, telling him the risk and letting him decide. Second person addresses WOLF.
lines.speaker: ENGINEER

lines.text:
The door goes. WOLF falls back
to wait for %s's call.
lines.context: Narration after the sealed door blows. %s is the engineer's first name; the possessive must work with any name. The line break is authored.
